rulings.challenge_claim: The only cross-seam device the row discloses at 10:2|10:3 (a shared fool-vocabulary root) is absent from the bytes, and the device that does straddle the seam (lev) goes unnamed.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the verse skeletons (consonantal tier). Eccl.10.2 carries כסיל for 'fool'; Eccl.10.3 carries סכל (twice, once inside the ketiv/qere pair). A skeleton sweep of כסיל returns 17 verses book-wide with 3 in ch10 (10:2, 10:12, 10:15); a skeleton sweep of סכל returns 11 verses book-wide with 5 in ch10 (10:1, 10:3, 10:6, 10:13, 10:14) — no ch10 verse carries both skeletons, so the two 'fool' words are consonantally distinct lexemes, not a shared root, confirming the challenge's core claim. Separately confirmed by direct skeleton-tier reading: Eccl.10.2 carries לב and ולב (heart, twice) and Eccl.10.3 carries לבו (his heart/mind) — a genuine lev-root recurrence across the row's own seam that neither the boundary_rationale nor strongest_rejected_alternative names, contrary to the standing cross-seam-cohesion disclosure rule. The single_saying call itself is unaffected: v.2 is a closed antithetic couplet and v.3 is a distinct narrative-conditional sentence, so the correct grounds support the same boundary, just not the grounds as written.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite strongest_rejected_alternative to drop the 'shared fool-vocabulary root' claim (consonantally false; כסיל and סכל are distinct skeletons with zero ch10 overlap) and replace it with the accurate device: the row and its neighbor share the לב root, not a fool root. Add a one-sentence device_notes disclosure of the lev recurrence (10:2 לב/ולב vs 10:3 לבו) with the argument that a common word repeated across a seam does not by itself force clustering, matching the sentence-zone single_saying default. Test the cure must pass: re-sweep כסיל/סכל skeletons in ch10 (must show zero overlap) and re-confirm the לב tokens are present in both verses at skeleton tier.

rulings.challenge_claim: The MT 10:3 ketiv/qere is correctly disclosed but mischaracterized as mere pointing variation when the two consonantal forms differ, and two neighbour-devices named in the row do not survive byte check.
rulings.grounds: Skeleton comparison of the inline ketiv/qere pair at Eccl.10.3 confirms a real consonantal difference: the ketiv skeleton כשהסכל is six letters and includes ה (the definite article, 'when the fool'); the qere skeleton כשסכל is five letters with no ה ('when a fool'/'as a fool'). This is a definite-vs-indefinite difference in the consonantal text, not a pointing-only variant, so the row's 'unpointed and pointed forms of when the fool [walks]' framing understates what is actually two different consonant strings. Separately, device_notes' 'lo/root repetition with v.2' claim does not resolve to any byte-real token: a search for the literal token לו returns no hits at Eccl.10.2 or Eccl.10.3 at either the byte or accent-stripped tier. As with the companion row, the boundary_rationale and strongest_rejected_alternative also lean on a 'shared heart and fool-root vocabulary' claim; heart (לב, confirmed at 10:2 and as לבו at 10:3) is genuinely shared, but the fool terms (כסיל at 10:2 vs סכל at 10:3) are distinct skeletons with no ch10 overlap between them. None of this disturbs the single_saying call itself, which rests independently on the verse being one complete conditional-temporal sentence.
rulings.remedy: Correct the K/Q characterization to state the consonantal difference explicitly (ketiv carries the definite article ה that the qere omits) rather than calling them simply unpointed/pointed forms of the same word. Remove or rewrite the unsupported 'lo/root repetition' clause in device_notes; if it was intended to reference the heart/fool vocabulary, correct it in parallel with the companion row's fix (lev genuinely shared; fool-lexeme not). Test the cure must pass: re-splice the ketiv (6 consonants, includes ה) against the qere (5 consonants, no ה) at skeleton tier, and re-run a literal לו token check at Eccl.10.2/10.3 (must return zero at both verses).

rulings.challenge_claim: The cluster's sole stated cohesion driver (v.6's asyndetic opening read as apposition) is the chapter's own default, is equally true of the excluded verse, and the two clustered verses share no content token at all.
rulings.grounds: Direct reading of all 20 MT ch10 verse openers confirms only Eccl.10.3 (וגם) and Eccl.10.14 (והסכל) open with a coordinating waw; the other 18, including both Eccl.10.6 and the excluded Eccl.10.7, open without one — asyndeton is the chapter's overwhelming norm and does not discriminate the row's own far boundary. Eccl.10.6 (נתן הסכל במרומים רבים) is a finite Niphal-perfect clause with its own subject and predicate, not a nominal standing in apposition to the unnamed 'error' of v.5 — 'apposition' mislabels the grammar. Content-token comparison across the span confirms Eccl.10.5 and Eccl.10.6 share zero tokens, while Eccl.10.5 and Eccl.10.7 both carry ראיתי (raiti, the book's I-saw observation formula, 18 sites book-wide per the device inventory, including both 10.5 and 10.7) — the one real lexical tie in this stretch pairs the row's own opening verse with the verse the row excludes, not with v.6. The chapter-exclusive תחת השמש refrain (the only ch10 site, per the device inventory's 27-verse tachat-hashemesh sweep) sits inside v.5 and marks the unit's own opening but is not disclosed as a device. Under the owner ruling that saying_cluster in a sentence zone requires byte-grounded cohesion evidence and that a driver that is really just the zone's default is over-clustering, this row's stated basis does not survive re-derivation.
rulings.remedy: BOUNDARY-CHANGE PROPOSAL (not self-executing; requires boss adoption): revert Eccl.10.5 and Eccl.10.6 to two single_saying rows under the sentence-zone default, since the sole named cohesion driver fails re-derivation and the one real lexical tie in the span (raiti) runs from v.5 to the excluded v.7, not to v.6. If a genuine construction-level tie between v.5 and v.6 specifically can be shown from bytes, the cluster may be retained with that corrected rationale instead. Test the cure must pass: re-verify ch10 verse-initial waw distribution (must show asyndeton is not distinctive), re-verify Eccl.10.5/10.6 zero content-token overlap, and re-verify the raiti tie runs 10.5-to-10.7.

rulings.challenge_claim: The stated four-fold template holds for the participles but not for the resumptive-pronoun harm-clause the row names as the cluster's cohesion object, and a book-exclusive nachash device straddling the row's closing seam is undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: Colon-by-colon parse of Eccl.10.8-Eccl.10.9 (skeleton tier) confirms the four participial openers (חפר, ופרץ, מסיע, בוקע) are genuinely uniform, so the cluster is not baseless. But the specific object the row names — participle-subject plus a resumptive-pronoun harm-clause — is 3 of 4, not 4 of 4: in cola 1, 3, and 4 (בו יפול; יעצב בהם; יסכן בם) the participle's referent remains the subject of the verb and a prepositional resumptive (בו/בהם/בם) points back to the object; colon 2 (ופרץ גדר ישכנו נחש) inverts this — the participle's referent is folded into the verb's own pronominal suffix (ישכנו, 'will bite him') while a new explicit subject, נחש, is introduced, and colon 2 is also the only one of the four cola that opens with a coordinating vav (the prefixed vav of ופרץ). Separately, a skeleton sweep of נחש returns exactly two verses book-wide, Eccl.10.8 and Eccl.10.11, sharing a bite-root (root letters נ-ש-ך) verb in both (ישכנו at 10.8, ישך at 10.11); a bare skeleton sweep of the unassimilated root letters נ-ש-ך returns zero verses because the prefixed imperfect assimilates the nun, so the tie is real but escapes naive substring sweeps. This book-exclusive pair straddles the seam between this row and the next and is not named in either row's device_notes.
rulings.remedy: Correct device_notes to state the template holds for 3 of 4 cola and name the outlier (colon 2 inverts subject/object roles and alone carries a coordinating vav) rather than asserting uniform four-fold symmetry 'without a shift in register.' Add a one-sentence cross-seam disclosure of the nachash/bite-root tie to Eccl.10.11, consistent with the campaign's cross-seam-cohesion rule; this is disclosure-only and does not by itself require reopening the 10.9|10.10 cut. Test the cure must pass: re-parse all four cola for subject/object role and vav-prefix, and re-sweep נחש (must return exactly Eccl.10.8 and Eccl.10.11).

rulings.challenge_claim: The repeated advantage keyword re-derives true and is uniquely adjacent, but the row's placement claim is not what the bytes show, its semantic bridge is translation-dependent, and a book-exclusive nachash tie back to v.8 across the row's opening seam is undisclosed.
rulings.grounds: A skeleton sweep of יתרון returns exactly 9 verses book-wide (1.3, 2.11, 2.13, 3.9, 5.8=web5.9, 5.15=web5.16, 7.12, 10.10, 10.11), one token each, and Eccl.10.10-10.11 is the only consecutive-verse pair among the nine — the recurrence is real and locally distinctive despite being common vocabulary elsewhere. But direct reading of the verse skeletons shows neither verse closes on it: Eccl.10.10 ends חכמה (two tokens after יתרון, past the disclosed ketiv/qere pair), and Eccl.10.11 ends הלשון (two tokens after יתרון) — the row's 'closes with'/'brackets both endings' language misplaces the keyword, which sits mid-clause in both verses. The 'skill applied too late' bridge is not itself a byte claim: בלוא לחש is a privative construction ('without a charm/whisper'); the temporal 'too late' sense comes from the WEB rendering ('before it is charmed'), not from the Hebrew syntax. A skeleton sweep of נחש confirms exactly two verses book-wide, Eccl.10.8 and Eccl.10.11 (ישך הנחש here, sharing the assimilated-nun bite-root with 10.8's ישכנו) — this book-exclusive pair straddles the row's own opening seam and is undisclosed. The K/Q disclosure at Eccl.10.10 itself is correctly spliced and met.
rulings.remedy: Rewrite the boundary_rationale to drop the 'closes with'/'brackets both endings' placement claim and instead state the confirmed, honestly-thin driver: יתרון is the only consecutive-verse pair among nine book-wide sites. Correct or drop the 'skill applied too late' gloss, or explicitly flag it as WEB-rendering-level rather than a claim on בלוא לחש's own syntax. Add the נחש/bite-root cross-seam disclosure symmetric to the preceding row's remedy. The medium_low confidence hold is appropriate and should be retained. Test the cure must pass: re-confirm יתרון's 9-site distribution and unique adjacency, re-confirm the verse-final position of חכמה/הלשון (not יתרון), and re-sweep נחש (exactly Eccl.10.8 and Eccl.10.11).

rulings.challenge_claim: The saying_cluster call overstates a keyword bracket that is actually Qohelet's own habitual thematic vocabulary, and omits a genuine, undisclosed cross-seam echo tying v.11 back to v.8.
rulings.grounds: The placement defect and the undisclosed nachash/bite-root tie to Eccl.10.8 are both confirmed real by independent byte re-derivation (see the companion OL ruling on this same row for the shared bytes) and are the SAME underlying defects both primaries independently found — convergent, not distinct. Where this item's framing overstates: it treats the 9-verse book-wide distribution of יתרון as proof the keyword is 'not a marker unique to this pair' and risks pure over-clustering. Re-derivation shows more precisely that Eccl.10.10-10.11 is the ONLY consecutive-verse pair among those 9 sites (verified by sweep), which is a genuine, if thin, local/structural signal and not merely a shared theme — consistent with the row's own honest medium_low confidence hold and with the toolkit's own expectation that this exact stretch would carry sub-2-token cohesion evidence. The corrected finding: the placement claim must be fixed (as this item and the companion OL item both require), but the keyword driver itself should not be dismissed as baseless.
rulings.remedy: Same remedy as the companion OL ruling on this row: fix the placement/'brackets' language, retain the keyword driver but reframed as 'the only consecutive-verse pair among nine book-wide sites' rather than a bracketing device, and add the nachash cross-seam disclosure. No boundary change proposed here — the cluster's evidentiary basis, once corrected, remains within the medium_low band the row already discloses.

supported_sample.notes: A skeleton sweep of the contiguous phrase דברי פי returns exactly 2 verses book-wide: Eccl.10.12 and Eccl.10.13, with no other site in the book. Confirms the row's central cohesion claim at the byte-derived skeleton tier.

supported_sample.claim_checked: המושל (with the definite article) at Eccl.10.4 is a hapax in Eccl, distinct from השליט at Eccl.10.5, which belongs to a 5-verse book-wide family.
supported_sample.notes: A skeleton sweep of המושל (definite form) returns exactly 1 verse book-wide, Eccl.10.4. A skeleton sweep of שליט (the shallit family) returns exactly 5 verses book-wide: Eccl.5.18(=web5.19), 6.2, 7.19, 8.8, 10.5. The bare (non-articled) מושל form also occurs once more at Eccl.9.17, but the row's claim was specific to the articled form, which is correctly a hapax.
